만나다.x: Let's meet in front of the school tomorrow.
만나다.e: 만나서 반가워요 = Nice to meet you (lit. 'glad because we met').
만나다.t: The person takes 을/를 or 하고: 친구를 만나요 / 친구하고 만나요.

걱정하다.forms: 걱정해요 · 걱정했어요 · 걱정할 거예요 · 걱정하지 마세요
걱정하다.x: My mom worries a lot about my health.
걱정하다.e: Drop 하다 to get the noun 걱정 'worry': 걱정이 많아요 = I have a lot of worries.
걱정하다.t: 걱정하지 마세요 'Don't worry' is one of the most useful phrases; casually, just say 걱정 마.

회의실.ex: 오후 두 시에 회의실에서 회의가 있어요.
회의실.x: There's a meeting in the conference room at 2 p.m.

느끼다.ex: 한국에서 처음으로 가을 날씨의 아름다움을 느꼈어요.
느끼다.x: In Korea I felt the beauty of autumn weather for the first time.
느끼다.e: The noun 느낌 'feeling' comes from 느끼- + -ㅁ.

자라다.x: I grew up in a small seaside village.

상을 받다.forms: 상을 받아요 · 상을 받았어요 · 상을 받을 거예요 · 상을 받은 (+noun)
상을 받다.m: to win a prize, to receive an award
상을 받다.ex: 제 친구가 글쓰기 대회에서 상을 받았어요.
상을 받다.x: My friend won a prize in a writing contest.
상을 받다.e: Literally 'to receive a prize'; 상을 타다 means the same.

깨달음.ex: 그 책을 읽고 큰 깨달음을 얻었어요.
깨달음.x: I gained a big insight from reading that book.
깨달음.e: Noun from 깨닫다 'to realize' (ㄷ irregular: 깨달아요).

탬버린.ex: 친구가 노래할 때 제가 탬버린을 쳤어요.
탬버린.x: I played the tambourine while my friend sang.
탬버린.t: Most 노래방 rooms have a couple; shaking one to cheer on whoever is singing is part of the fun.

엉엉.x: The child fell down and cried loudly.
엉엉.e: 의성어 (sound word) for loud, open crying. Its bright-vowel partner 앙앙 is a small child's wail.
엉엉.t: Almost always paired with 울다: 엉엉 울다 'to bawl'. Quiet sniffling is 훌쩍훌쩍.

일시불.m: lump-sum payment, paying in full at once
일시불.x: Please put it on my card as a single payment.
일시불.e: Literally 'one-time payment' — the opposite of paying in installments (할부).
일시불.t: At Korean stores the cashier often asks 일시불로 해 드릴까요? — pay in full or in installments?

제보자.x: The informant did not reveal their name.
제보자.e: Literally 'a person who offers a report.'

저리다.m: to go numb, to tingle (pins and needles); to ache (heart, figurative)
저리다.x: I sat for a long time, and now my legs have fallen asleep.
저리다.e: Also figurative: 가슴이 저리다 means 'my heart aches' with sadness.
저리다.t: Don't confuse it with 절이다 'to salt, pickle' — both are pronounced [저리다].

초음파.ex: 임신 중에 초음파로 아기를 처음 봤어요.
초음파.x: During my pregnancy, I saw the baby for the first time on an ultrasound.
초음파.e: Literally 'beyond-sound wave' — sound too high to hear.

기후 변화.ex: 기후 변화로 농사짓기가 점점 어려워지고 있습니다.
기후 변화.x: Farming is getting harder and harder because of climate change.
기후 변화.t: 기후 is long-term climate; 날씨 is the weather today.

쓰나미.ex: 지진 후에 쓰나미가 해안 마을을 덮쳤어요.
쓰나미.x: After the earthquake, a tsunami struck the coastal village.
쓰나미.e: From Japanese 'tsunami'; the official Korean term is 지진해일.

아쉬움.m: regret, disappointment; a sense that something is missing
아쉬움.x: The trip was so short that I'm left wishing it had been longer.
아쉬움.e: Noun from 아쉽다 'regrettable, wanting': ㅂ becomes 우, then -ㅁ is added.
아쉬움.t: 아쉬움 is a mild 'too bad, I wish there were more', not the heavy guilt of 후회.

하여튼.x: Anyway, let's talk again tomorrow morning.
하여튼.e: From 하여 'how' plus -튼 (from 하든 'whether'): 'however it may be'; 여하튼 swaps the first two syllables.

가리다.m: to cover, to hide, to block (from view); to be picky about, to tell apart
가리다.x: The child covered her face with her hands out of shyness.
가리다.e: Homonym warning: 'cover, hide' and 'pick, be choosy' are both 가리다.
가리다.t: Set phrases: 음식을 가리다 = to be picky with food; 낯을 가리다 = to be shy with strangers.

굶다.m: to skip a meal, to go hungry, to starve
굶다.x: I was so busy that I skipped lunch today.
굶다.t: Pronounced [굼따] — in ㄻ only ㅁ is heard before a consonant.

권하다.m: to recommend, to suggest; to offer (food, drinks)
권하다.x: The doctor recommended that I exercise every day.
권하다.e: Literally 'do urging': 권 means to urge or encourage.
권하다.t: 술을 권하다 means offering someone a drink, a big part of Korean drinking etiquette.

인과 관계.ex: 흡연과 폐암 사이에는 인과 관계가 있습니다.
인과 관계.x: There is a causal relationship between smoking and lung cancer.
인과 관계.t: Don't confuse 인과 관계 (causation) with 상관관계 (correlation) in reading passages.

경기력.x: Our team's performance has improved a lot.

육상.x: My younger sibling came in first at the school track meet.
육상.e: Literally 'on land' — sports on land, as opposed to swimming.

욕망.ex: 끝없는 욕망은 사람을 불행하게 만들 수 있어요.
욕망.x: Endless desire can make a person unhappy.

국왕.x: The British king made an official visit to Korea.
국왕.t: 국왕 is the formal, news-style word; in stories and casual talk 왕 is more common.

걸림돌.ex: 높은 비용이 사업 확장의 걸림돌이 되고 있어요.
걸림돌.x: High costs are becoming an obstacle to expanding the business.
걸림돌.e: From 걸리다 'to get caught' + 돌 'stone': a stone your foot catches on.
걸림돌.t: Pronounced [걸림똘]; it is the direct opposite of 디딤돌, and the two are often paired in speeches.

사과문.ex: 논란이 커지자 그 가수는 SNS에 사과문을 올렸어요.
사과문.x: As the controversy grew, the singer posted an apology on social media.
사과문.e: Literally 'writing that apologizes for a fault'; 사과 'apology' is unrelated to 사과 'apple'.
사과문.t: Typical verbs: 사과문을 발표하다 (issue) or 사과문을 올리다 (post online).

오름세.ex: 채소 가격이 계속 오름세를 보이고 있어요.
오름세.t: Pronounced [오름쎄]; a friendlier native synonym of 상승세, common for prices.

양적완화.ex: 중앙은행은 양적완화를 통해 시장에 돈을 풀었습니다.
양적완화.x: The central bank released money into the market through quantitative easing.
양적완화.t: Often shortened in news to QE; the opposite policy is 양적긴축 'quantitative tightening'.

평가절상.ex: 위안화가 평가절상되면 중국 제품 가격이 오를 수 있어요.
평가절상.x: If the yuan is revalued, prices of Chinese goods may go up.

모회사.ex: 모회사가 자회사의 빚을 대신 갚아 주었습니다.
모회사.x: The parent company paid off its subsidiary's debt.
모회사.e: Literally 'mother company'; a subsidiary is a 'child company,' 자회사.

유신론.ex: 유신론은 세상을 창조한 신이 있다고 믿는 입장이에요.
유신론.x: Theism is the position that a god created the world.
유신론.e: Literally 'there-is-a-god theory'; 유 and 무 (have/lack) are a common opposite pair.

모멸감.m: humiliation, feeling insulted or looked down on
모멸감.ex: 사람들 앞에서 무시를 당해서 모멸감을 느꼈어요.
모멸감.x: I felt humiliated after being ignored in front of people.

섭정.ex: 어린 왕 대신 대비가 섭정을 했어요.
섭정.x: The queen dowager ruled as regent for the young king.
섭정.e: Literally 'taking over government' on someone's behalf.

백중지세.m: an even match, neck and neck
백중지세.ex: 두 후보의 지지율이 백중지세를 보이고 있습니다.
백중지세.x: The two candidates are neck and neck in approval ratings.
백중지세.e: Literally 'like first and second brothers' — hard to tell who's ahead.
백중지세.t: The synonym 막상막하 is more common in speech; 백중지세 suits news and sports commentary.

여하간.m: anyway, at any rate, in any case
여하간.ex: 여하간 이번 주 안에는 꼭 끝내야 해요.
여하간.x: At any rate, we have to finish it within this week.
여하간.t: Synonyms 어쨌든, 아무튼, 하여간; 여하간 sounds a bit more formal and old-fashioned.
